method.selection: Highest 3 local excursions and highest 3 absolute errors among detected peaks; union with worst-error step and immediate neighbors, per cohort. Selection frozen before execution.
method.inputs: 3 CPU episodes of 512 steps, 15 native warm-up steps each. Original physical frames reproduced exactly, ignoring clocks and request UUID hashes. Selected input tensors and baseline predictions retained as NPZ.
method.counterfactual: Recompute remaining residual from the original input and baseline pressure; execute exactly one learned pass, using the existing corrector. Do not advance the simulation with that pressure.
method.oracle: Existing separable spectral pseudoinverse for the sealed Neumann operator, checked against the independent explicit-neighbor action at relative defect < 1e-9. Reference is the solution for this exact AI request, not the independently evolving reference trajectory in the drift plot.
method.precision: Original float32 neural weights and forward pass; unchanged existing float64 physical residual/reconstruction/oracle arithmetic. CPU only.
method.timing: One discarded warm-up repetition plus 3 measured pairs per capture. Baseline is model correction and stopping checks; incremental extra includes residual reconstruction, one neural pass and final stopping-quality calculation. Excludes IPC and simulator advancement. Independent workers pinned to CPUs [20, 21, 22], each one Torch thread.
method.resource_policy: Immutable model packages in separate processes; 8589934592 bytes available-memory reserve; native deadline 600 s and worker deadline 1200 s. Existing rollout owns native termination/reaping; worker cancellation raises through that owner.

findings: 54/54 tested inputs improved in absolute error; 54/54 improved in mean-free same-request error. Selected drift-peak steps: 17.
Median same-request pressure error reduction at selected peak steps: C45: 84.7%, C53: 87.6%, C55: 85.9%.

Median reduction in neighboring/context inputs: C45: 85.6%, C53: 85.5%, C55: 86.1%. The comparison shrinks current-solve errors but does not establish disappearance of the phase-dependent drift pattern.
Some peaks in independently evolved trajectory error are not peaks in same-request pressure error. Accumulated state differences and pressure-gauge effects remain distinct from current-solve error.
The model can still contract these small residuals after the existing stopping rule accepts them; this is not an irreducible current-solve error floor in these cases.
This paired test does not establish improved full-trajectory drift, deployment readiness, or a general model ranking. No weights, training, acceptance thresholds or deployed solver changed.
next_step: Run a separately labelled closed-loop comparison using adaptive stop plus exactly one extra pass, with unchanged scene inputs and physical limits. Measure drift, worst-step accuracy and complete step runtime before adopting the policy or selecting new training feedback.
